answer: A river of fake accounts can only be dammed at its inlet: require every identity to enroll a handwritten signature, captured as stroke order and pressure. Each epoch the network issues a fresh phrase to write by hand; no two hands write alike, and timing jitter plus pen lifts form a fingerprint no script can forge, since the phrase changes every epoch. A farm with a hundred puppets needs a hundred real writers on call, paid, while an honest user writes one line. Forged copies collapse into one cluster and burn the bond, so every extra identity costs the same, and the river of clones dries up.
